clauses.reason: whole: Executive Order No. 9165 of May 19, 1942 "is hereby" revoked (printed 'is hereby revoked' at the end of one line). The order states no effective date, so the revocation was performed on signing, April 18, 1944; the filing date, April 20, 1944, is not used. The command is exhausted by performance and EO 9165 stays revoked. The second paragraph, which begins "This order shall not be deemed to", limits what the revocation terminates and adds no continuing command.

research_rationale:
EO 9437 (signed April 18, 1944; F.R. Doc. 44-5654, filed April 20, 1944) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. It revokes EO 9165 of May 19, 1942 (protection of essential facilities from sabotage and other destructive acts) and adds a sentence that the order does not terminate War Department facility security functions or preclude cooperative arrangements with the agencies named in paragraph 3 of EO 9165. The order states no effective date, so the revocation was performed on signing, 1944-04-18, and the order is exhausted by performance; EO 9165 stays revoked as a surviving consequence. The second paragraph is a limit on what the revocation terminates, not a separate command, and is kept within the single scope. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.
